title: OT Connector Configuration
description: TOML configuration for a tedge-dot instance, expressed as JSON Schema. Protocol-specific objects (connection, device.protocol_address, point.address) are validated by each connector's own schema.

service_name.description: Connector service name; defaults to 'tedge-dot-<protocol>'. It addresses the connector's management commands (te/device/main/service/<service>/ot/cmd/<verb>/<id>), so it must be unique on the broker and cannot be changed by set-config.

operation_timeout.description: Upper bound on a single protocol-module call (read batch, write, connect, subscribe). A module that never returns — what a half-open socket produces: no answer, no error, no reset — would otherwise block the connector's loop forever, stopping samples, health and link status with nothing logged. The runtime turns the bound into an ordinary transport error, so the usual degraded-link and reconnect handling applies.

stall_timeout.description: How long the connector's loop may make no progress before it is treated as wedged and restarted (the supervisor cancels and re-runs it; the MQTT last will marks the service down). Must exceed operation_timeout; "0" disables the watchdog.

point_library_path.description: Directories searched for the point libraries devices name in points_from (§3.4), most specific first. REPLACES the default path (/etc/tedge/plugins/ot/points.d then /usr/share/tedge-dot/points.d), so it must name at least one directory; omit the key to use the default. Relative entries resolve against this configuration file's own directory.

connection.description: Protocol-specific shared connection defaults. Shape defined by the connector spec.

disabled_device.description: A device switched off with enabled = false (§3.3). The connector reads nothing but its name and the names of its keys, so this schema requires nothing more of it; fields it does carry are still checked for shape.

type.description: The device type this instance is one of (§3.1): what its point list describes, not where it is. Inherited from the first point library named in points_from that declares a [library] type (§3.4) when absent here. It qualifies the device's parameter set names (§5.2), which are tenant-wide identifiers in the cloud, and is echoed in every sample and on the link status.

protocol_address.description: Protocol-specific device address. Shape defined by the connector spec.

enabled.description: false takes the device out of the configuration (§3.3): it is not connected, polled, described or answered for, and nothing else about it is read — not even its point libraries. The definition stays in the file (and a management command can switch it back on); its name still counts for uniqueness.

points_from.description: Point libraries this device inherits its points from, in order (§3.4). An entry containing '/' or ending in '.toml' is a path (relative ones resolve against this configuration file's directory); anything else is a name, resolved as <dir>/<protocol>/<name>.toml along the library search path. Libraries are applied in order and then the device's own inline points, with a repeated id patching what came before: meta and transform merge key by key, every other field replaces.

allOf.description: A disabled device (enabled = false) is not loaded, so nothing but its name is required of it (§3.3); every other device needs an address.

Without a points_from reference there is nothing for a point to inherit from, so every inline point must be complete (§3.4). With one, a point may be a patch and the connector applies these rules to the resolved point instead — which a static schema cannot check, since it would have to read the referenced files. A disabled device is not loaded (§3.3), so its points are not checked either.

name.description: Short human-readable label for this signal, for wherever a name is displayed instead of the id — which is a topic segment and a parameter-set key, so it stays a plain identifier. Feeds a parameter's DTM title and the capability descriptor's point_labels (§7). Not echoed per sample.

description.description: Longer human-readable explanation of the signal. Feeds a parameter's DTM description and the capability descriptor's point_labels (§7). Not echoed per sample; meta.parameter.description overrides it for the parameter UI.

address.description: Protocol-specific point address. Shape defined by the connector spec.

transform.description: Linear engineering transform applied by the connector after decode: (value * multiplier * 10^decimal_shift / divisor) + offset.

meta.description: Free-form signal metadata, echoed verbatim as 'meta' in every sample envelope for this point. Never interpreted by the connector; flows read it for per-signal behaviour (e.g. on_change, deadband, min_interval, debounce) and consumers may carry arbitrary descriptive fields.

subscribe.description: Set false to keep this point on the polling schedule even when the connector supports push delivery (subscriptions).

point.description: A point definition. When the device inherits points from a library (§3.4) this may be a patch of one: only `id` is required, and any field it omits keeps the inherited value. A device that inherits nothing must define every point completely, which $defs/complete_point states.

complete_point.description: The completeness rules a point must satisfy when nothing supplies its missing fields: a full address, and a datatype whenever the mode is typed (§3.3).

point.name: Boiler temp
point.description: Outlet temperature after the heat exchanger
